Terms of Service

Last updated: 17 November 2026

These terms are an agreement between you and Hardouch Anas, who runs Relay (“we”, “us”). By creating an account or using Relay you accept them. If you don't agree, please don't use Relay.

1. Who can use Relay

  • You must be at least 16 years old. We ask for your date of birth when you sign up and check it on our server.
  • You must not have been banned from Relay before, and using Relay must be legal where you live.

2. Your account

  • Keep your password private and turn on two-step verification if you can. You're responsible for what happens in your account.
  • Choose a username and display name that don't pretend to be someone else.
  • You can download your data or delete your account at any time in Settings.

3. Acceptable use

Follow the Community Guidelines. In short, don't use Relay to:

  • harass, threaten, bully or impersonate anyone;
  • share content that sexually exploits children, promotes terrorism or violence, or is otherwise illegal;
  • send spam, scams, malware or phishing links;
  • share someone's private information or intimate images without their consent;
  • attack, overload, scrape or try to break into Relay or other people's accounts.

4. Your content

Messages, photos, voice notes, stories and other things you share stay yours. You give us only the permission we need to store them, deliver them to the people you send them to, and show them in the app. You confirm you have the right to share them.

Secret chats are end-to-end encrypted: we can't read them. Other chats are stored on our servers and, as explained in the Privacy Policy, the site owner can review them, for example to investigate a report.

5. Moderation and termination

We may remove content, restrict, suspend or delete accounts that break these terms or the law, or that put others at risk. Where we can, we tell you why. If you think we got it wrong, contact us (section 10) and we'll look again.

6. Third-party content

Some features show content from other services (for example YouTube videos, music previews, radio stations and podcasts). That content belongs to its owners and is covered by their own terms.

7. Relay is provided “as is”

Relay is a personal, free project. We work to keep it available and secure, but we can't promise it will always be available, free of errors, or that messages will never be lost. Keep your own copy of anything important.

8. Limitation of liability

To the extent the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for content other people share. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under consumer-protection law that can't be limited.

9. Changes

We may update these terms. If a change matters, Relay will ask you to accept the new version before you continue. The date at the top shows the latest version.

10. Law and contact

These terms are governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Morocco, without affecting mandatory rights you have where you live. Questions: github.com/Anas2103/Relay/issues.
